interfaces should be passed by span so these can be passed by a consexpr array.  They're not required to be sorted, so we shouldn't take the hit for sorting at every call site.

Yeah, apparently `std::span` does not work with the `std::flat_set`. Changed it to flat_set here.

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58300580/why-are-flat-set-and-flat-map-not-contiguousrange

changed it to flat_set.

But flat_set does not implicitly convert to a span so that invalidates some other comments.

See https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58300580/why-are-flat-set-and-flat-map-not-contiguousrange
Please don't forward declare classes like this.  Just #include the things you need.

It's a cyclic include if i were to do this.

I don't like it either but did not want to do any further refactoring for these simple function extractions.

Let me know if it's still blocking and what specifically you would like to see in terms of moving functions around / new headers / ... to resolve this issue.

> Just #include the things you need.

Closing this comment since the suggested fix simply does not work (creating cyclic include and build failure).

Please let me know if you have a concrete idea for how to fix the cyclic dependency between `PerformProbe` and `PerformScan`. Anywho, if we find a solution for that, it will not be in scope for this patch (which is about extracting a helper function for object mapper usage).

> creating cyclic include and build failure)

Then fix that?

forward declarations aren't a replacement for defining cyclical headers.  If the headers have a cycle, rearrange code until you no longer have a cycle.

Also, please don't just close out comments because they inconvenience this patch.

This is also documented in the coding guidelines:

https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#sf9-avoid-cyclic-dependencies-among-source-files

putting async_method calls in their own compile unit can cause template duplication issues, because this same code might be compiled in multiple units.

Can you unpack this template duplication issue for me?

Don't the `async_method_call` usages we have all have different callback types?

So we will need to instantiate the template multiple times anyways, right?

The usages we have
- GetSubTree
- get host state
- properties GetAll

What do you suggest? I don't think it's appropriate to put all those in a `dbus_utils.cpp` since it's different usages.

Should we perhaps explicitly instantiate the templates we use and then put that into `dbus_utils.cpp` or something like that?

Something like
`async_method_call_variant_string_type`
`async_method_call_getsubtree_type`
`async_method_call_getall_type`

That would keep it at least somewhat independent of usage semantics and then we can compile all those together and add others as needed. Let me know 😊
